assessment: In this manuscript, the authors show that DNMT3A is essential for the regulation of adipocyte lipolysis and organismal metabolism. Focusing on a mouse model with heterozygous null mutations in DNMT3A, as seen in Tatton-Brown-Rahman syndrome in humans, the authors show that animals develop obesity with adipocyte hypertrophy. Using a combination of single cell analysis, additional genetic models, and bisulfite sequencing, the authors propose a mechanism whereby DNMT3A regulates adipocyte differentiation and overall metabolism. This well-written paper will be of broad interest to researchers studying metabolism, development, and epigenetics.
